title: Rearchitecting the Datacenter Lifecycle for AI
extraction_scope: Author preprint abstract and accessible sections; no independent reproduction or reviewer verdict.

identity.limit: Preprint is primary technical evidence but is not independently reviewed here.

mechanism: A lifecycle framework jointly co-optimizes AI datacenter building, hardware refresh, and operation decisions under workload growth, hardware evolution, and system aging.

conditions.baseline: Traditional lifecycle policies and a baseline deployment timeline
conditions.simulation: Monte Carlo simulations over workload growth, model scaling, hardware availability, and cost projections
conditions.representative_datacenter: 10 MW, approximately 500 H100 servers, 75% average utilization, roughly 70 GWh annual operating energy
conditions.workload_assumptions: AI inference demand and model-size growth scenarios; linear, sub-linear, and accelerated growth cases
conditions.operational_scope: Power, cooling, networking, hardware refresh, model migration, quantization, KV-cache management, disaggregation, routing, and scheduling

reported_results: The abstract reports up to 40% TCO reduction versus traditional approaches.
The preprint reports stage-specific and cross-stage savings under modeled scenarios, including sensitivity to refresh and workload-growth policies.
limits: Results are modeled projections, not measurements from a deployed datacenter.
TCO depends on assumed demand growth, hardware availability, prices, energy, and cooling parameters.
The reported percentage is not transferable to every datacenter or workload without matching assumptions.
Independent review and reproduction remain pending.
next_action: Reconcile the preprint against the published paper, capture the exact figures/tables and sensitivity ranges, then prepare independent review.
